pages.quiz:
MUSIC AND DANCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: MUSIC AND DANCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Best practice when working on Contemporary Songs from Kenya: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Contemporary Songs from Kenya with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Contemporary Songs from Kenya.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Contemporary Songs from Kenya.
   D. Damage equipment used for Contemporary Songs from Kenya.

2. Best practice when working on Four-Part Harmony: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Four-Part Harmony with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Damage equipment used for Four-Part Harmony.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Four-Part Harmony.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Four-Part Harmony.

3. In music, tempo refers to: (1 mark)
   A. The ticket price
   B. The speed of the music
   C. Only the costume
   D. Only the volume

4. Best practice when working on Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble.
   D. Damage equipment used for Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble.

5. Best practice when working on Dance Production: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Dance Production.
   B. Practise Dance Production with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Dance Production.
   D. Damage equipment used for Dance Production.

6. Best practice when working on Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.
   D. Practise Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

7. Primary colours are: (1 mark)
   A. Brown, pink, and gold
   B. Green, orange, and purple
   C. Black, white, and grey
   D. Red, blue, and yellow

8. Warming up before sport helps to: (1 mark)
   A. Guarantee a trophy
   B. Replace drinking water
   C. Remove the need for rules
   D. Prepare muscles and reduce injury risk

9. Best practice when working on Western Ensembles: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Western Ensembles.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Western Ensembles.
   C. Damage equipment used for Western Ensembles.
   D. Practise Western Ensembles with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

10. Best practice when working on Instrumental Transpositions: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Instrumental Transpositions.
   B. Damage equipment used for Instrumental Transpositions.
   C. Practise Instrumental Transpositions with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Instrumental Transpositions.

11. Best practice when working on Rhythm: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Rhythm.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Rhythm.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Rhythm.
   D. Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

12. Best practice when working on Western Instruments: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Western Instruments.
   B. Practise Western Instruments with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Western Instruments.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Western Instruments.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Setting Text to Music and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Four-Part Harmony and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Music Notation Software. and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Dance Production and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Practise Contemporary Songs from Kenya with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

2. A — Practise Four-Part Harmony with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

3. B — The speed of the music

4. A — Practise Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

5. B — Practise Dance Production with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

6. D — Practise Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

7. D — Red, blue, and yellow

8. D — Prepare muscles and reduce injury risk

9. D — Practise Western Ensembles with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

10. C — Practise Instrumental Transpositions with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

11. D — Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

12. B — Practise Western Instruments with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Setting Text to Music; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Four-Part Harmony; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Music Notation Software.; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Dance Production; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
